_about: SHELF of French classics in English before 1931, works no other shelf holds: Racine's plays (Boswell's metrical version, 1890-97), Froissart's Chronicle in Lord Berners's Tudor translation (1523-25; Ker's Tudor Translations, 6 vols, 1901-03), Commines's Memoirs (Scoble, Bohn 1855-56), Thierry's Norman Conquest (Hazlitt, 1847), Saint-Simon's Memoirs (Bayle St. John, Gutenberg), and (added round 100) Sainte-Beuve's Portraits of Women and of Men and Monday-Chats, Maurice de Guérin's Journal Senancour's Obermann twice, and (round 101) Taine's On Intelligence (Haye). Each title gates on its own translator. Printings before 1931 only. US public domain. Added 2026-10-17 by lane C (round 96); Adam may veto. No uids minted.

_excluded.froissart-johnes: Thomas Johnes's Froissart (1848) goes on the johnes shelf, not here.
_excluded.boys-froissart: Lanier's Boy's Froissart and similar condensations for young readers are adaptations of Johnes, not new translations.
_excluded.thierry-merovingian-1841: Narratives of the Merovingian Era (Whittaker, 1841): the only scan found has no text layer.
_excluded.sainte-beuve-select-essays-butler: A. J. Butler's Select Essays of Sainte-Beuve (Edward Arnold; selectessaysofsa00sainuoft): the scan's title page carries no date and the catalogue record none either, so the printing cannot be shown to precede 1931.
